The evidence supports the claim that larger pinhole sizes increase transmittance (by noting that small pinholes result in low transmittance, implying larger ones would be higher) and that this setup enables wide viewing angles. It does not state that the calculation burden increases 'linearly' with pinhole size or number in the manner suggested by the claim (which implies a negative trade-off regarding computational complexity scaling with aperture size/number in a way that compromises the system). In fact, the text highlights the efficiency of the calculation relative to the mode space. Therefore, the specific claim about the linear increase in calculation burden is not supported and potentially contradicted by the emphasis on computational efficiency.
